title: mapping-bioimage-software: data and code for Mapping bioimage-analysis software adoption in microscopy
description: Data and code for Mapping bioimage-analysis software adoption in microscopy. The registry contains 33 entries: 23 analysis packages, six microscope-control programs, MATLAB and Jupyter notebooks as references, Adobe Photoshop for figure preparation and NIH Image for historical counts. The 29-package aggregate combines the 23 analysis packages with six microscope-control programs. References, Photoshop and NIH Image are excluded. After about 2000, many “NIH Image” mentions refer to ImageJ. The deep-learning series uses 13 core analysis packages. Jupyter notebooks retain their aliases, notebook category and core scope. The original 14-package calibration sample remains frozen, and the three new-package precision samples are stored separately. The archive holds processed counts, annotator-labelled validation sets, identifier-only sampling frames, configuration, code and provenance. Data sources: Europe PMC (search API and open-access full text; metadata derived from MEDLINE/PubMed carries the NLM notice that the data may not be current and that NLM does not endorse this work; full text was mined and never redistributed), OpenAlex (CC0), the GitHub REST API (public repository counts), pypistats.org (30-day PyPI download totals from the Python Software Foundation's PyPI BigQuery dataset, CC BY 4.0), the image.sc forum (topic counts only, no posts), Crossref and ORCID (bibliographic metadata, CC0), and MeSH headings from MEDLINE records (2026 MeSH vocabulary, retrieved 15 October 2026). The archive contains no article titles, abstracts or full text. Article text can be rebuilt from identifiers with release/refetch_identifiers.py through Europe PMC. The data are licensed under CC BY 4.0 (LICENSE-DATA) and the code under MIT (LICENSE); this record carries CC BY 4.0 for the data and states the MIT licence for the code. Albin Johansson Professorship); the Kavli Foundation co-funds the EOSS Cycle 6 award.
